Moved off Friday: the doc skips this on purpose as minor, and notes the Castle Circuit ticket stays valid the next day if you want it back.
Moved off Friday: the doc routes down Nerudova instead, to reach the Torto pastry stop. Gardens close for the season on 1 Nov and run ~10:00-18:00 in October.

Changing of the guard, First Courtyard, 12:00 daily - fanfare, flag exchange, drills, ~15 min. Dropped from Friday to make room for the 13:00 Lobkowicz concert and a real lunch; it needs 11:45 arrival for a view, so it costs 30 min not 15. Sentries change hourly at the gates anyway, so you will likely catch a simpler one in passing.

Grand cafe on Vitezna, one of Prague's best and not a tourist room. Considered for Friday lunch but passed over for Baracnicka rychta, which is closer to the Old Castle Steps and gets you eating ~15 min sooner. Book ahead if you go.

The Bartered Bride (Smetana) was the Saturday night plan - dropped because the remaining seats were either expensive or cheap with bad sightlines. The building itself is worth ten minutes if you pass it; the interior only opens to ticket holders.

21 galleries, 90 min audio tour, ~360-590 CZK. Dropped: it costs more than the National Gallery joint ticket (300 CZK for Schwarzenberg AND Sternberg) for a weaker painting collection, and reviews call it family-portrait heavy - 'little work of major interest'. Its unique assets are Beethoven's hand-annotated manuscripts, Mozart's re-orchestration of Handel's Messiah, and Bruegel the Elder's Haymaking (one of the surviving Seasons cycle). Worth 60 min on a free afternoon if the Bruegel or the manuscripts pull you. The 13:00 daily concert here runs to 830 CZK as a combo, 600 alone.

ops.insert: Vladislav Hall (largest secular Gothic hall in central Europe) and the defenestration window. ~30 min. Dropped to fit Sternberg onto Friday: the two National Gallery palaces cannot open before 10:00 and need ~3h together, so only one hour is left for the castle interior before them. Covered by the same 450 CZK Castle Circuit as St Vitus, so it costs nothing extra if you have time in the free afternoon.

place.name: Letenský zámeček a zahrádky na Letné
Vinice a Vinotéka sv. Kláry - Botanická zahrada Praha

ops.insert: Local institution hidden in a courtyard off Trziste, Mala Strana. Cheap, Czech, no tourist markup. Was Friday lunch until the day was rebuilt around Schwarzenberg - Bistro Loreta is now 5 min from the gallery, where Baracnicka rychta is a 15 min walk downhill. Still the better pick if you would rather eat in Mala Strana.

Plum poppyseed strudel and a savory snek, weekdays to 17:00, no seating. Lazenska 15, Mala Strana. Dropped from Friday once lunch moved to 14:30 - a pastry straight after a late lunch is one stop too many. Easy to slot back in if you skip a sit-down lunch.
Moved off Thursday: the doc's arrival lunch is Mr. Banh Mi on Rumunska, six minutes from the hotel, rather than crossing to Old Town to eat.

House-brewed lagers on Korunni 106, open to midnight. Was Friday dinner. Swapped for Vinohradsky Parlament once the plan moved from beer to Moravian wine: the brewery has exactly ONE wine by the glass (Pinot Chardonnay Sedlak, 89 Kc) and it is a white, wrong for game. Still the better choice if you want beer - their Vinohradska 11 svetly (72 Kc/0.5l) and Black Panda tmavy (75 Kc) are house-brewed and distinct from Lokal's tank Prazdroj and U Fleku's 1499 dark.
Grilled pork banh mi, 6 min from the hotel; fast, which suits an arrival day.

place.name: National Gallery Prague - Convent of St. Agnes

ops.insert: Kolace specialist that doubles as a bookshop, open to 18:00. Order poppyseed and plum, white poppyseed, tvaroh with blueberry.
groceries, open to 21:00, on the way to the metro. Mattoni (neperliva = still), Studentska pecet, kefir, nakladany hermelin. Bring a tote; bags cost extra.
walk through the courtyard en route to St Giles, then down Karlova and left onto Husova.
20:30 walk back. Lit up and half empty at this hour, then Metro A home from Staromestska.
07:45 breakfast, opens 07:00. Makovy and tvaroh kolace, black coffee. TAKE A CHLEBICEK FOR YOUR POCKET

Old Masters I: Cranach, Durer, El Greco, Holbein, Gossaert, Rubens, Spranger, Brandl. On Hradcanske namesti, the public square OUTSIDE the castle gates - no security queue, no Circuit ticket. Opens 10:00 (Tue-Sun). Joint ticket 300 CZK also covers Sternberg on Saturday, bought on the day at either ticket office.

Old Masters II, 3 min across the square from Schwarzenberg. Durer's Feast of the Rose Garlands (1506), plus Rembrandt, Goya, the Brueghels, Tintoretto, Ribera, Tiepolo, Bronzino. The stronger of the two collections. Opens 10:00 Tue-Sun; same 300 CZK joint ticket as Schwarzenberg.
5 min west of Schwarzenberg. Hidden courtyard with a fountain. Duck burger; ask what the daily soup is first, it is sometimes a beef broth. ~330 CZK.

16:00, opens exactly then. Mon-Fri 16:00-22:00, CLOSED Sat and Sun - the only window on this trip. 5 min from the hotel on Budecska 29, 4.8 stars. NOT a bottle run: carry-on only means wine cannot come home from a shop (liquids over 100ml fail security). It is a proper wine bar as well as a vinoteka, so treat this as a tasting - ask them to walk you through Moravian varieties, which also sets you up for the Frankovka at dinner. If you do want wine home, the only route is airside duty free at PRG on Sunday (sealed bag, direct flight so no re-screening), and the Moravian selection there is thin.

21:45 dinner, Korunni 1 - the Namesti Miru end, so closer to both the opera and the hotel than the brewery. Open to midnight. BOOK AHEAD (9700+ reviews, Friday night). ORDER: Danek na vine a smazeny konfit - fallow deer in red wine, parsnip puree, croquette of pulled venison - 285 Kc, plus 2x Frankovka 0.15l at 99 Kc = 483 Kc total. Every wine by the glass is Moravian (Arte Vini, Znojemsko + Velkopavlovicko): Veltlinske zelene 79, Svatovavrinecke 79, rose 89, Rulandske sede 99, Frankovka 99. Alternatives: kachni prso (duck, cherry sauce) 325; jeleni kyta (red deer + unlimited dumpling and sauce degustation) 355. NO BEEF - avoid the Friday special (rozznena spicka hoveziho orechu 379), tatarak 305, hovezi rozbif 265, obri spanelsky ptacek 345, striploin 475, houbovy knedlik s hovezim zebrem 295, and the beef-rib broth. Their beer is tank Prazdroj, same as Thursday's Lokal, so wine is the better call here.

place.name: Farmers' Saturday market
place.formatted_address: Rašínovo nábřeží Vltavská, Náplavka, 120 00 Praha 2, Czechia
place.vicinity: Rašínovo nábřeží Vltavská, Náplavka, New Town

ops.insert: 08:15 breakfast. Saturdays 08:00-14:00, 90+ vendors. Kolace, smoked meats, fried fish, serious coffee. Ask for burcak (mid-Oct is the tail of the season). Homemade wine is marked domaci. Go early before the stalls jam.
13:45 lunch. Dark 13 lager brewed on site since 1499, not sold anywhere else, plus a pork dish. ~400 CZK. Wave off the accordion player and the herbal shot.

place.name: Crème de la Crème - zmrzlinový salon

ops.insert: 16:20 vineyard walk (Grebovka), 15-18 min on foot. Loop up through the vines and the grotto. West-facing slope at golden hour.

Wine pavilion at the top of the vines, open to 22:00, west-facing. With the opera dropped you can now stay for the actual sunset at 18:10 and the twilight to ~18:45, which is the whole point of the west slope. Czech wine by the glass - ask for a Ryzlink rynsky or a Frankovka. It is outdoors and mid-October evenings run 6-8C, so bring the shell and a layer.
22:15 dinner after the opera, open to midnight. Wine rather than beer: cheese and cold cuts plate with two glasses of Moravian. Ask what sparkling is open. ~450 CZK.

placeMetadata.description: Museum showcasing a collection of medieval paintings & statues in a 13th-century Gothic monastery.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The National Gallery Prague - Convent of St. Agnes is a museum located in a 13th-century Gothic monastery, showcasing a remarkable collection of medieval paintings and statues from Bohemia and Central Europe. The convent, situated in the northeastern corner of Stare Mesto, is the oldest surviving Gothic building in Prague and has been restored for its current use by the National Gallery.

placeMetadata.name: Farmers' Saturday market

placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The Farmers' Saturday Market in Prague is a popular spot for locals and tourists alike, offering a wide variety of local produce, baked goods, pottery, and crafts. Located on Naplavka Street overlooking the river, this market provides a picturesque setting with views of the river and Prague Castle. With a rotating roster of vendors, visitors can enjoy quality breakfast options such as baked goods, sandwiches, and galettes while taking in the charming atmosphere.

placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Ferdinanda is a traditional Czech restaurant located in the center of Prague, offering classic Czech dishes and a variety of local beers. The restaurant is known for its affordable and hearty meals, including popular options like pork knuckles, authentic goulash, and crispy schnitzel with fries. The bright and airy interior creates a welcoming atmosphere for enjoying Czech cuisine and local beer without breaking the bank.

placeMetadata.name: Bobsleigh Kutna Hora

The bobsleigh track provides a thrilling ride, with the option to go down twice without braking. The karts are also a popular attraction, offering fun for both kids and adults. Visitors can enjoy picturesque views of the city and nature while experiencing the excitement of the tracks.

The cathedral, with its sharp spines and flying buttresses, is a UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the most well-preserved churches in Central Europe. It was built between 1257 and 1281 and boasts five naves. The construction began in 1388 but wasn't completed until the early twentieth century. St.

placeMetadata.name: Mr. Banh Mi
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Mr. Banh Mi is a Vietnamese restaurant that specializes in delicious Banh Mi sandwiches, along with rolls, soups, salads, and rice and noodle dishes. Despite its small size, the eatery offers a warm and tasty dining experience at affordable prices compared to other nearby establishments. It's worth noting that their bread closely resembles the authentic taste found in Vietnam. While waiting times can be slightly longer due to it being a family-run business, the clean environment adds to the overall appeal.

placeMetadata.name: House of the Black Madonna
placeMetadata.description: 5-story historic building with Cubist architecture offering works of Czech Cubism & an opulent cafe.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The House at the Black Madonna is a 5-story historic building in Prague, showcasing remarkable Czech Cubist architecture. Designed by Josef Gocar, it houses the small Czech Museum of Cubism and the Grand Cafe Orient, featuring an array of Cubist artifacts. The building's construction from reinforced concrete is an engineering marvel, blending into Prague's historical Old Town despite its unique style. Additionally, visitors can explore nearby attractions on a walking tour to discover more of the city's best Cubist buildings.

placeMetadata.name: MATOKA Georgian, Bakery & Coffee ☕🍰
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: MATOKA Georgian, Bakery & Coffee is a charming bakery that offers a delightful selection of pastries and baked goods. The flaky pastry topped with cream and raspberries provides a sweet and tart indulgence, while the glazed croissant-like delight with crushed pistachios offers a rich, nutty flavor. These treats showcase the bakery's expertise in blending traditional baking with gourmet finesse. Additionally, the honey cake is praised for its subtle sweetness and freshness.

placeMetadata.name: U Fleků
placeMetadata.description: Famous historic venue with 8 separate dining halls dishing out traditional local dishes & beer.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: U Fleků is a historic venue in Prague, dating back to 1499 and renowned as the only brewery and restaurant in Central Europe that has been brewing continuously for over five centuries. It offers traditional Czech and Bohemian cuisine, including roast pork knuckle, garlic soup, and apple strudel. The establishment comprises eight distinct dining halls with unique decor, as well as an inner beer garden accommodating up to 500 people.

Altán Grebovka
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: If you're looking for a scenic spot to enjoy a glass of wine, Vinicni altan is perfect. The restaurant is perched atop a vineyard in Pragues second-largest park, and the gazebo structure allegedly set up by Emperor Charles IV makes for an elegant setting. You can try wines from the vineyard below as well as further-reaching Czech varieties here.

placeMetadata.name: The Powder Tower
placeMetadata.description: City gate built in the 15th century and restored after being damaged in the Battle of Prague.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The Powder Tower, known as Prasna Brana, is a stunning Gothic structure that dates back to the 15th century. Originally one of the thirteen gateways to Prague's Old Town, it served a crucial role in the city's defense by storing gunpowder. After suffering significant damage during the Battle of Prague in 1757, it was beautifully restored in the 19th century and now features an eye-catching trapezoidal roof.

placeMetadata.name: Loreto
placeMetadata.description: Historic pilgrimage destination with a church, a cloister, a clock tower & rare liturgical objects.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Loreto in Prague is a significant pilgrimage site with a rich history and religious significance. It features a church, cloister, and clock tower, as well as rare liturgical objects. The complex is associated with the Holy Shack, believed to be the house in Nazareth where the Virgin Mary received the prophecy of the Savior's birth.

placeMetadata.name: State Opera
placeMetadata.description: Elegant gilded stage with an illustrious history & a world class opera & ballet program.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The Prague State Opera, also known as the Former New German Theatre, is a historic and elegant venue with a rich cultural legacy. Built in 1888, it offers world-class opera and ballet performances. Managed by the National Theatre, this neo-Renaissance building boasts a gilded stage and breathtaking interior. Despite its unfortunate location across from a major highway, it remains one of Central Europe's most important music venues.

placeMetadata.name: Šternberský Palace
placeMetadata.description: Art museum in a palace, home to ancient Greek & Roman works, Renaissance and 19th-century paintings.

placeMetadata.name: Grébovka (Havlíčkovy sady)
placeMetadata.description: Peaceful Italian Renaissance–style park with a pond, fountain, statues & a charming artificial cave.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Grébovka, also known as Havlíčkovy sady, is a tranquil Italian Renaissance–style park located in the charming neighborhood of Vinohrady in Prague. This spacious park offers a peaceful retreat with its pond, fountain, statues, and an enchanting artificial cave. It is larger and less crowded than some other city-center parks, providing ample space to escape the hustle and bustle of festivals or events.

placeMetadata.name: Sisters Bistro v Dlouhé
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The Sisters Bistro v Dlouhé is a cosy bistro with a delicious menu that includes egg salad and parma ham sandwiches. The bakery attached makes it easy to access delicious sweets. It's the perfect place for a breakfast, small snack, or full meal.

placeMetadata.name: Bánh Mì Makers - Smíchov
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Banh Mi Makers in Smíchov City is a must-visit for lovers of Vietnamese street food. The restaurant offers iconic banh mi sandwiches and other delightful dishes like pork bun, fresh rolls with mango, bun bo hue, and pho veggie. The spacious and modern outpost provides friendly service and delicious food, making it a definite culinary gem worth revisiting. With its cozy interior, fast service, and generous portions, this spot is perfect for those craving authentic Vietnamese cuisine.

placeMetadata.name: Italian Court Kutna Hora
placeMetadata.description: Museum of coin minting in a 1400s former royal palace with elegant chapel & ornate Audience Hall.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The Italian Court in Kutna Hora, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is a former royal palace that now houses a museum of coin minting. This 1400s building features an elegant chapel and an ornate Audience Hall. The town itself boasts stunning Gothic architecture, including the magnificent St. Barbara's Church and the Italian Court, which was once used as the royal mint for producing the famous Prague groschen.

placeMetadata.name: Lobkowicz Palace
placeMetadata.description: Baroque palace containing the art collection of the Lobkowicz family, including many Old Masters.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Lobkowicz Palace, located within the Prague Castle area, is a Baroque gem housing the impressive art collection of the Lobkowicz family. The private collection includes Old Masters' artworks, musical instruments, manuscripts, and historical artifacts such as Beethoven's handwritten scores and original compositions by Mozart. Visitors can gain insight into the creative process of these famous composers through these exhibits. The museum offers a personalized experience with an audio guide narrated by relatives from the Lobkowicz family.

placeMetadata.name: Libeřské lahůdky
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The deli Libeřské lahůdky is a local favorite, known for its incredible selection of chlebicek (sandwiches), as well as creams and sandwiches. The staff are friendly and the prices are very reasonable. This deli can be found near The National Museum in Old Town, and is always busy due to its great food and friendly atmosphere.

placeMetadata.name: Old Town Square
placeMetadata.description: Oldest square in the historic center with 10th-century origins, site of many Gothic buildings.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Old Town Square, located in the heart of Prague, is a historic and picturesque square with origins dating back to the 10th century. This UNESCO-listed site has retained its medieval charm and serves as a hub for visitors seeking to immerse themselves in the city's rich history and vibrant atmosphere. The square is adorned with an array of architectural marvels, including Gothic buildings like the Old Town Hall and the iconic Prague Astronomical Clock.

placeMetadata.name: Vinohradský Parlament Restaurant
placeMetadata.description: Airy bar & restaurant for modern takes on classic Czech specialties, plus beer & craft beverages.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Vinohradský Parlament Restaurant is a popular spot for modern twists on classic Czech dishes and a wide selection of beer and craft beverages. It's known for its airy atmosphere, making it a hit with families due to the attached playroom. The restaurant offers contemporary versions of traditional Czech cuisine, such as plum-filled potato dumplings and fruit dumplings garnished with cottage cheese and melted butter.

placeMetadata.name: Albert
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Nestled beneath the bustling Desiried Department Store in Wenceslas Square, Albert Supermarket is a gem for both locals and tourists alike. While it may take a bit of searching to locate this popular spot, once you do, you'll find a clean and well-organized space stocked with everything from groceries to household essentials. The staff are friendly and eager to assist, making your shopping experience pleasant.

placeMetadata.name: Old Royal Palace
placeMetadata.description: Late Gothic palace in Prague Castle, with Renaissance elements & Vladislav Hall for royal events.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The Old Royal Palace, located within Prague Castle, is a stunning late Gothic palace with Renaissance elements. It features the impressive Vladislav Hall, where royal events were held. The palace has a rich history as the residence of Czech monarchs and Bohemian princes throughout the centuries. Its architectural transformation from a simple wooden building to encompassing various styles such as Gothic, Romanesque, Renaissance, and Baroque is truly remarkable.

placeMetadata.name: The Estates Theatre
placeMetadata.description: Continuously running since 1783, an elegant theater presenting opera, ballet & dramatic works.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The Estates Theatre, part of the National Theatre family, is an elegant and historic venue in Prague that has been running since 1783. It gained fame for hosting the world premiere of Mozart's Don Giovanni opera in 1787 and has continued to stage important Czech opera and drama productions.

placeMetadata.name: National Theatre
placeMetadata.description: Magnificent venue for nationally sponsored new & classical ballet, opera & theater performances.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: The National Theatre, also known as Narodni Divadlo in Czech, is a significant cultural institution in Prague. It holds a rich artistic tradition and is considered the Alma Mater of Czech Opera. The venue showcases nationally sponsored new and classical ballet, opera, and theater performances. Situated just a five-minute walk from the hotel, this historical late 19th-century building boasts magnificent interiors that are truly captivating.

placeMetadata.name: Municipal house
placeMetadata.description: Art nouveau venue hosting classical concerts, opera & ballet plus events including fashion shows.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Obecní Dům, also known as Municipal House, is a stunning art nouveau venue in the heart of Prague. This architectural gem took seven years to build and now stands as one of the most beautiful buildings in the Czech Republic. It boasts a 2,000-seat concert hall, salons, offices, and restaurants adorned with lavish decorative work. The venue hosts classical concerts, opera, ballet performances, and various events like fashion shows.

placeMetadata.name: Café Savoy
placeMetadata.description: Refined cafe/restaurant with a lavish wooden interior evoking the First Czechoslovakian Republic.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Café Savoy is a sophisticated café and restaurant exuding an old-world charm, featuring a lavish wooden interior reminiscent of the First Czechoslovakian Republic. Locals flock to this European-style café for its delectable brunch offerings, including fresh croissants, Prague ham, and creamy coffee served beneath ornate high ceilings adorned with designer chandeliers.

placeMetadata.name: Klementinum
placeMetadata.description: Complex comprised of the Mirror Chapel & Baroque Library, with Atlas atop the Astronomical Tower.
placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Klementinum is a historic complex located at the eastern end of the Charles Bridge, featuring the Mirror Chapel, Baroque Library, and an Astronomical Tower with an Atlas statue. Originally a Jesuit dormitory in the 16th century, it expanded to include a library, university, and scientific institutions. Guided tours showcase its opulent areas such as the Baroque library adorned with frescoes, Meridian Hall, and the Astronomical Tower offering stunning city views.

placeMetadata.name: Holešovice Market

placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Holešovice Market, also known as Prague Market, is the city's largest year-round marketplace located within a former abattoir and cattle market dating back to the Austro-Hungarian era. The complex features a variety of stalls offering fruit, vegetables, flowers, herbs, spices, cheese, baked goods and more. It is a lively mix of Czech farmers selling local produce in Hall 22 and Vietnamese stands offering diverse products.

placeMetadata.name: Jerusalem Synagogue

placeMetadata.generatedDescription: Nestled in the heart of Prague's New Town, the Jerusalem Synagogue is a hidden gem that beautifully showcases a blend of Art Nouveau and Moorish architectural styles. Inaugurated in 1906 and designed by Wilhelm Stiassny, this stunning structure stands out with its vibrant colors and intricate facade, making it an ideal spot for photography enthusiasts. While exploring the city’s rich Jewish heritage, don’t overlook this architectural marvel tucked away on a quiet side street.
